extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of 19th-century travel/exploration narratives; naturalists, naval officers, and general readers interested in Australian exploration and maritime surveying
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit standards for producing a descriptive exploratory travel narrative that mixes navigational data, natural history, ethnographic observation, and lyrical scene-setting. Emphasizes precise measurements, specimen records, practical recommendations, and reflective commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precise geographic coordinates and measurements
rubrics_metrics.description: Record exact positions and measurements: latitudes, longitudes, bearings, depths, and distances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in text: 'My position was in latitude 17 degrees 58 1/2 minutes South longitude 7 degrees 12 1/2 East of Port Essington, or 139 degrees 25 minutes East of Greenwich'; numerous bearings and depth soundings are given throughout. Use numerical precision to locate features and support navigational claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed tidal and tidal-stream information
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the character and timing of tides and tidal streams, rise at springs and neaps, and peculiarities of local tidal behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text provides specifics: 'The tides in the head of the Gulf of Carpentaria appear to be a compound of many others... producing only one tide in 24 hours.' Footnotes give times, directions, and amplitudes (e.g., springs 9 to 12 feet, neaps 3 to 8 feet). Include flood/ebb directions, durations and strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigation and safe-passage guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Give practical instructions for navigating channels, bars, and inlets: bearings to take, conditions when channels are passable, and signs to guide a ship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'When the eastern part of this clump of trees bears South 45 degrees West, and Kangaroo Point South 10 degrees West the bar will have been passed' and 'the bar can only be taken at high-water springs.' Provide actionable bearings, depths, and landmarks for mariners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report of hazards and obstructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe impediments to progress (fallen/sunken trees, shoals, reefs, driftwood) and how they affect travel or navigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative notes progress impeded 'by fallen or sunken trees' and shoaling near islands; warn readers of likely stoppages, dangers to small boats, and where ascent or further advance may be impossible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural history inventory and specimen counts
rubrics_metrics.description: List flora and fauna observed, often with counts and localities (game book style).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text enumerates birds, fish and mammals and presents a game-book extract (e.g., 'Booby Island (June and August) 145 quails, 18 pigeons...'). Include species lists, relative abundance, and where specimens were taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of scientific names and specimen annotation
rubrics_metrics.description: When possible, give scientific names or taxonomic notes and make clear when a species is rare or newly observed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Footnote example: 'Cacatua eos' for rose-coloured cockatoos and mention of 'Macropus unguifer' as a rare kangaroo. Record provenance of specimens and any uniqueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative economic/trade reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide descriptions of local commerce including goods, volumes, and value estimates for imports and exports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author gives estimates: 'each Bughis proa imports to the amount of from 10,000 to 30,000 dollars' and aggregate approximations. Include lists of traded items (pearls, tortoise-shell, calico) and infer economic significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical logistical recommendations for exploration
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer pragmatic suggestions for future expeditions (transport, equipment, staging points).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example recommendation: 'A few camels, with skins for conveying water, would be the means of effecting this great end in a very short time.' Propose specific resources, staging locations (e.g., Investigator Road), and methods to accomplish objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soil and land-quality observations with expert corroboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess soil quality and agricultural potential and, when possible, consult or cite expert opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The passage: 'the soil ... according to one so well qualified to judge as Sir W. Hooker ... is of a rich quality.' Provide physical description of soil, comparison with other areas, and mention expert assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Climatic and meteorological data
rubrics_metrics.description: Record temperatures, barometric readings, wind directions, diurnal ranges and seasonal notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: thermometer ranges (51 to 87 degrees), barometer readings, wind patterns (South to South-East in July), and diurnal temperature differences. Present both specific readings and general seasonal patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological journaling of movements and events
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a dated log of actions, anchoring, landings, and notable incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative marks dates (e.g., 'August 4', 'June 23') and links them with precise actions. Maintain chronology so readers can follow campaign progression and temporal context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of illustrations, plates, and charts
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference and include visual materials (views, plates, charts) to complement descriptive text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author refers to 'the view in the beginning of the first volume' and 'see the view annexed' and mentions charts 'accompanying this work.' Use maps and plates to clarify landscapes, routes and observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethnographic and cultural observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe interactions with local peoples, their customs, burial practices, institutions (church), and trading behaviour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: description of Booby Island cemetery, visits from village schoolmaster and chiefs, and native behaviour aboard ship. Report cultural encounters respectfully and informatively, noting customs and social organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anecdotal human-interest reporting (accidents and consequences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Record incidents affecting personnel (injuries, deaths) and their operational consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The account of Mr. Fitzmaurice's ankle injury and its impact ('he was maimed for life') illustrates including human cost. Use such anecdotes to convey risk and real costs of exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of lyrical description and empirical detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine evocative, sensory prose with factual, empirical reporting to render place while informing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of lyrical language: 'moonlight broke ... in showers of silver' contrasted with soundings and bearings. Use vivid imagery for atmosphere yet preserve technical accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-referencing and engagement with prior authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Compare observations with earlier explorers' reports and recent surveys to corroborate or dispute positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text references Flinders and Captain Blackwood to validate or question known positions ('as the reader will perceive' and 'confirms my opinion'). Cite prior work and reconcile differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording of place-names and naming rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide local names, newly assigned names, and the reasons or incidents leading to those names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Kangaroo Point... was seen a large light-coloured kangaroo, which ... afforded us a name.' Give coordinates and context for naming decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Game-log / hunting records
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep organised enumerative records (game book) of species captured, with dates and locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The included game-book extract lists species counts by place and month. Maintain such logs systematically to support natural-history claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical assessment of anchorage and vessel suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Note depths, widths and conditions to assess whether harbours and channels suit certain vessels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements like 'This was highly satisfactory, as it proved there was water for the largest vessels' and 'The Albert is navigable, for vessels of a draught suited to the bar, thirteen miles' illustrate evaluating navigability and anchorage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of footnotes for technical elaboration and correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide supplementary technical details, clarifications, and digressions in footnotes rather than interrupting narrative flow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple footnotes supply tidal data, species names, and chart references. Use footnotes to house dense technical data, cross-checks, and authorial asides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting agricultural and resource potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess prospects for settlement, farming and resource exploitation, including timber and cultivation notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author speculates on timber export potential and agricultural promise ('The Plains of Promise', 'trees... highly spoken of by the Bughis'). Include observations on resources and potential uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observations on seasonal variation and its effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Note how phenomena (water salinity, inlets carrying fresh water, presence of proas) vary by season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: inlets may contain fresh water in rainy season; Malay proas 'occasionally visit the southern shores... and fill fresh water' at certain times. Record likely seasonal dynamics and their operational implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of comparative geological/geomorphological observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Make observations about land formation, presence or absence of rocks, pebbles and what this suggests about drainage and history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text remarks 'We met no rocks during our walk; a porphyritic pebble or two being the only stones noticed... showing that the water by which they were carried had a slow motion.' Use geomorphological evidence to infer landscape history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly state limitations and uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge when data are incomplete, when examination was cursory, and when conjecture is speculative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author writes 'we were obliged to have recourse to the pump every hour' and 'for the day soon closed in, leaving only the pale light of the moon to guide us' and also 'All I could do was to give one long lingering look... it not being permitted me to clear up this point.' Flag uncertainties and limits to investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide instructions for future surveys and staging
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend specific staging locations and methods for future work (e.g., put flat-bottomed boats together and tow them, use Investigator Road as a port).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'The expedition should... go to Investigator Road... the flat-bottomed boats, taken out in frame, for the purpose of carrying up the camels, should be put together, and towed from thence to the river.' Offer logistical sequences and infrastructure suggestions.
